title: The constant square-zero residue and its truncation counterexample
statement: Let ell be prime, k a separably closed field, X=Spec k, and Lambda the discrete continuous condensed ring A=Z/ell^2. Let P be the cokernel of ell times the identity of the regular condensed Lambda-module, and M its monoidal inverse image to X. Then M is constant-model constructible, M[0] has no finite Tor amplitude, and there exists a bounded constant-model constructible complex K of finite Tor amplitude such that truncGE_0(K) has no finite Tor amplitude. The assertion is invariant under a specified condensed coefficient-ring isomorphism, so it is stated for an abstract commutative condensed ring isomorphic to the continuous finite ring.

source.place: The examples, constant-sheaf specialization and the two-term truncation counterexample

proof.text: The annihilator of ell in Z/ell^2 is the ideal (ell). Use the periodic multiplication-by-ell free resolution of F=A/(ell). After tensoring with F all differentials vanish, so each nonpositive tensor homology module is F. Constant sheafification, its finite-discrete ring comparison, and scheme inverse image identify the quotient with the displayed internal cokernel.

Constant F is nonzero on the nonempty scheme Spec k: nonzero constant sections cannot vanish after any jointly surjective cover. Thus the periodic tensor computation contradicts every finite lower Tor bound. The same finite scalar presentation exhibits M as a finite constant model on the identity cover and the one-stratum stratification.

Take the cone of multiplication by ell on the regular module in degree zero. Its two terms are finite free and its cohomology in degrees -1 and 0 is M. Thus it is bounded constructible and has Tor amplitude [-1,0]. Its upper truncation at zero is M[0], which has no finite Tor amplitude by the preceding calculation.

Transport along the specified coefficient isomorphism. Exact monoidal scalar restriction preserves the regular module, its integer-scalar endomorphisms, their cokernels, the finite constant presentations and the derived tensor interval. The inverse equivalence reflects finite Tor amplitude and commutes with the canonical truncation, so all three conclusions transfer.

lean.statement:
theorem constant_square_zero_tor_example (ℓ : ℕ) [Fact ℓ.Prime]
    (Λ : Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{0}) Ab.{1})
    [MonObj Λ] [IsCommMonObj Λ]
    (hΛ : Nonempty (Mon.mk Λ ≅
      Mon.mk (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj.{0} (ZMod (ℓ ^ 2)))))
    (k : Type) [Field k] [IsSepClosed k] :
    let X : Scheme.{0} := Scheme.Spec.obj (Opposite.op (CommRingCat.of k))
    let C := Mod (Sheaf (coherentTopology Profinite.{0}) Ab.{1}) Λ
    let P := cokernel ((ℓ : ℕ) • (𝟙 (𝟙_ C)))
    let Cₓ := Mod (Sheaf (Scheme.ProEt.topology X) Ab.{1}) (condensedRingObj Λ X)
    let M : Cₓ := ((upperStarFromPoint X).mapMod Λ).obj P
    IsConstantModelConstructible Λ X M ∧
    ¬ _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ
      ((_root_.DerivedCategory.singleFunctor Cₓ 0).obj M) ∧
    ∃ K : DerivedCategory Cₓ,
      (constantModelBoundedConstructible Λ X ⊓
        _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ) K ∧
      ¬ _root_.DerivedCategory.finiteTorAmplitude Cₓ
        ((_root_.DerivedCategory.TStructure.t.truncGE 0).obj K)
